note: The overlay adds two literal groups to register 6 (`foretag`) beside the artifact's `dodsorsak-forsta`. `artal-person` claims artal-person-1/2/3 (raw stem `artal-person-`); the peer artal-person4/5/6 (raw stem `artal-person`, other names) trims to the same key, and both fold, so the families case (no such scope) skips the pair as a trim collision. `foo` claims foo4/5/6 (raw stem `foo`), named Apples, Oranges and Cars: a battery, so the accepted family no longer folds; the peer foo-1/2/3 (raw stem `foo-`) does, and the families case emits it as `foo`. Run 1 names `partial`, the tree that built the artifact less those two groups: `dodsorsak-forsta` is still an accepted scope there, but its key is not the stem `dodsorsak`, so dodsorsak1 stays out and dodsorsak2-3 fold on their own, but the members of the two undeclared groups stay excluded, so each peer's key collides with a materialized group's key: no `artal-person` or `foo` family, three key collisions (`first`, register 4's edge group, as in the families case; `artal-person`; `foo`), no trim collision, and the families case's 11 families less `foo`. Run 2 names the tree that built the artifact, where both are accepted scopes: `artal-person` re-emits with its own three members, claimed as one block from its header to the blank line after its last member (the peer is rejected, no trim collision is counted); for `foo` the accepted subgroup is the winner and is dropped as a battery, so nothing is emitted under `foo` and foo-1/2/3 never surface. Counts: the families case's 11 families plus `artal-person` less `foo`, batteries q1-3 and foo4-6, the one key collision `first`.
